# Security & Input Validation Checklist: Taskify Kanban Board

**Purpose**: Check that the security and input-validation requirements are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before implementation. Covers spec.md, plan.md and the design artifacts (research.md, data-model.md, contracts/), measured against the constitution's NON-NEGOTIABLE Principles I and II.
**Created**: 2026-10-04
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Does the spec itself contain a threat assessment covering authentication, authorization, data exposure and abuse cases, or does that exist only in the plan? Constitution Principle I requires it in both. [Gap, Spec §Requirements, Plan §Threat assessment]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are validation rules (type, format, length, allowed values) specified for every input field, including optional descriptions, IDs in routes, and query parameters, and not only for names, titles and comments? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, §FR-009, §FR-015, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are validation rules defined for the inputs added by planning: notification mark-read/mark-all-read requests, hub method arguments, and `/internal/events` envelopes? [Gap, Research §R10, Contracts realtime-hub.md, events.md]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is the set of characters that are allowed in text fields specified (for example control characters, null bytes, bidirectional overrides, emoji), or is "any Unicode" the explicit rule? [Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK005 - Is the unit of the length limits defined (characters, grapheme clusters, UTF-16 code units or bytes)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-009, §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK006 - Are requirements for which audit events must be logged complete? Do they cover user switches, comment edits and deletes, and inter-service authentication failures, and not only "rejected requests and changes"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022, Research §R13]
- [ ] CHK007 - Are audit-log retention, access control and tamper-protection requirements specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are rate-limit thresholds (requests per window, per key such as IP, acting user or API key) and the response when a limit is exceeded quantified? [Gap, Research §R9, Constitution §Security Requirements]
- [ ] CHK009 - Are security-header requirements (CSP directives, frame policy, HSTS max-age) stated precisely enough to review, and not only as a list of header names? [Clarity, Research §R9]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are secret rotation requirements for the per-caller API keys documented, including how often keys rotate and how two keys overlap during a rotation? [Gap, Research §R8, Plan §Complexity Tracking D2]
- [ ] CHK011 - Is a request-body size limit specified for every API, separately from the per-field limits? [Gap, Spec §FR-019]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK012 - Is "a clear message that does not reveal internal details" defined, for example by listing what may and may not appear in an error (field names, limits, stack traces, IDs)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is "trusted internal environment" defined in a way that can be checked, such as named network boundaries, the rule that only the Web resource is exposed, or allowed source ranges? [Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Constraints]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is "displayed as plain text" defined for every place user text is output: board cards, task details, comment placeholders, notification summaries, page titles and attribute values? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is the order of trimming and validation stated for every text field? Is it also stated whether the stored value is the trimmed value or the original input? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-009, Research §R7]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is "permanently remove its text" defined in terms of storage, for example whether the text is also removed from outbox rows, backups and logs? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK017 - Is the meaning of "rejected" given a single definition for authorization failures, such as 403 versus 404 for a comment not owned by the user, and for stale versus foreign references? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, §FR-021]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK018 - Is the spec's assumption "live updates are not required" reconciled with the plan's real-time requirement (≤2 s), and is the spec updated to match? [Conflict, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Summary]
- [ ] CHK019 - Does the spec define notifications, now that they are added by the plan (R10) but listed as out of scope in the spec, so that their security requirements can be traced? [Conflict, Spec §Assumptions, Research §R10]
- [ ] CHK020 - Does treating the event payload as trusted ("Taken from trusted event payload") agree with Principle II's rule that internal origin does not imply trust? [Conflict, Data-model §Cross-service references, Constitution §II]
- [ ] CHK021 - Are the requirements that events carry task titles consistent with FR-022's data-minimization intent? Is it documented which fields may cross service boundaries? [Consistency, Contracts events.md, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK022 - Are comment ownership rules (FR-017) consistent with an identity that can be spoofed (any user can be selected, and `X-Taskify-User` is supplied by the client)? Is this limitation stated explicitly as accepted risk D1? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017, Research §R8, Plan §D1]
- [ ] CHK023 - Do the length limits match across spec, data model, OpenAPI contracts and client-side form rules? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-009, §FR-015, Contracts *.yaml]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK024 - Is the "test set covering each validation rule" in SC-005 defined well enough to count as complete, for example one accepted case and one rejected case per rule and per boundary? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK025 - Is the "test set of common injection inputs" in SC-006 specified or referenced (for example the OWASP XSS cheat sheet categories, with contexts listed)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK026 - Are there measurable acceptance criteria for audit logging, such as which fields must appear and the rule that no content fields are present? [Gap, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK027 - Are there acceptance criteria showing that the status history really cannot be changed? [Measurability, Spec §FR-023, Plan §Threat assessment]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK028 - Are requirements defined for a request with a missing, malformed or unknown acting user (the `X-Taskify-User` header), and for a selected-user cookie that is stale or tampered with? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Research §R8]
- [ ] CHK029 - Are requirements defined for duplicate or replayed write requests (double submission of create task or post comment)? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK030 - Are requirements specified for concurrent conflicting edits to a task's title, description or assignee (last write wins, or a conflict error)? Only concurrent moves are covered today. [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK031 - Are requirements defined for editing or deleting a comment that is already deleted, or that is deleted while another user is viewing it? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK032 - Are requirements defined for a user accessing or marking another user's notifications (for example a mark-read request with someone else's notification ID)? [Coverage, Gap, Research §R10]
- [ ] CHK033 - Are requirements defined for a real-time hub join with IDs the user should not observe, or for projects or tasks that do not exist? [Coverage, Contracts realtime-hub.md]
- [ ] CHK034 - Are failure and recovery requirements defined for when an internal API is unavailable, covering the user-facing error, partial writes and outbox delivery? [Coverage, Recovery Flow, Gap]
- [ ] CHK035 - Is the behavior defined for data written by a phase-1 spoofed identity once real authentication arrives in phase 2? [Gap, Assumption, Plan §D1]

## Non-Functional Security Requirements

- [ ] CHK036 - Are encryption-at-rest requirements for the PostgreSQL databases and backups specified, or explicitly scoped out for phase 1? [Gap, Constitution §I]
- [ ] CHK037 - Are least-privilege requirements for database roles stated per service and per table (for example no UPDATE/DELETE on status history)? [Completeness, Plan §Constitution Check]
- [ ] CHK038 - Is the 30-day notification retention requirement, and the deletion it implies, traced to a spec requirement? [Traceability, Data-model §Notification]
- [ ] CHK039 - Are requirements defined for what must happen if phase 1 is accidentally exposed publicly, such as detection, a kill switch or IP allow-listing? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK040 - Is the end of deviations D1 and D2 tied to a dated milestone or owner, as the constitution's accepted-risk rule requires (owner and review date)? [Assumption, Plan §Complexity Tracking, Constitution §Security Requirements]
- [ ] CHK041 - Is the assumption that the Product Manager role grants no extra rights stated as a requirement that can be tested, so that role-based authorization cannot be added by accident? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
